title: Shifting a Linear Graph Down and Right
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: The graph of y = (1/2)(x + 1) + 5 is to be shifted down 5 units and right 1 unit. Give a simplified equation for the shifted graph.

steps.title: Apply the Horizontal Shift (Right 1 Unit)
steps.explanation: Replace x with x - 1 to shift the graph 1 unit to the right; inside the parentheses, (x - 1) + 1 simplifies to x.
steps.why: Replacing x with x - 1 undoes the +1 horizontal offset inside (x + 1).

steps.title: Apply the Vertical Shift (Down 5 Units)
steps.explanation: Subtract 5 from the output to shift the graph 5 units downward, canceling the +5 constant term.

steps.title: Compare the Original and Shifted Lines
steps.explanation: The original line passes through (-1, 5) with slope 1/2 (y-intercept (0, 11/2)). Shifting right 1 and down 5 moves the point (-1, 5) to the origin (0, 0), giving the parallel line y = (1/2)x.
steps.why: Translating the point (-1, 5) by (+1, -5) maps it to (0, 0) while preserving slope 1/2.
